perspective:
**Carolyn Abebe’s available information / subjective perspective:**

- I work with Marilyn Olson at a community bank. We recently started working together and are still getting to know each other.
- During a busy week at the bank, I noticed Marilyn was unusually quiet and withdrawn for several days. This seemed unlike her normally engaging demeanor.
- I asked Marilyn if everything was alright and whether she wanted to talk. She told me she was a bit overwhelmed with work and some personal stuff, and thanked me for asking.
- In a later interaction, Marilyn was curt with me. I felt confused and slightly hurt.
- I told Marilyn I hoped I hadn’t overstepped, that I’d had tough times too, and that talking can sometimes help. She said she appreciated it, apologized if she seemed off, and said it had been a hard week.
- After that, Marilyn appeared to respond positively. I felt relieved and hopeful about our budding friendship.
- I invited Marilyn to a small get-together with friends that weekend. She said it sounded lovely, thanked me, and said she would love to join.
- Despite friendly interactions outside work, I felt Marilyn was still maintaining a professional distance at the bank. I felt disappointed.
- I asked to talk about our work dynamic and told her I felt there was a distance I couldn’t understand. Marilyn said she didn’t realize that, apologized if it seemed that way, and agreed to talk about improving our collaboration.
- After our private meeting, I believed we had cleared the air and better understood each other’s professional expectations and personal boundaries. I felt content and optimistic.
- I proposed teaming up on the new project proposal. Marilyn said that was a great idea, that she was glad we had that talk, and that she looked forward to working more closely with me.

**Not available to me:** Marilyn’s private thoughts, motives, or the actual details of her personal situation, except what she chose to tell me.
